lesson.title: Summaries that tell the truth
lesson.subtitle: Mean, median and range, and honest charts

video.title: Summaries that tell the truth
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma — the maths teacher (main character)
Mr Joseph — the computer studies teacher (cameo)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Average: 2 GB; Most of us: under 1; Both true?. Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: An advert says the average customer uses two gigabytes of data a month. Our class checked: most of us use less than one. How can both be true?

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: mean, median and range, and summaries that tell the truth.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Mean: add, then divide; Median: the middle, sorted; Range: biggest minus smallest.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here are three ways to sum up numbers. The mean: add them all, and divide by how many. The median: sort them, and take the middle one. The range: the biggest minus the smallest.

scenes.visual: A bar chart that draws itself: 1, 1, 2, 3, 9 (Gigabytes used in a month).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Five friends' data in a month: one, one, two, three and nine gigabytes. The mean is three point two. The median is two. One heavy user drags the mean up; the median stays put.

scenes.visual: Two columns: “Mean” (Numbers are similar) and “Median” (A few are far away).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So which should you use? The mean, when the numbers are similar. The median, when a few are far from the rest, like incomes, house prices or data use.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Marks of eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, and one typed as one hundred and fifty. Which summary is still about right?

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: The median: thirteen. The mean jumps to forty, which is impossible for marks out of twenty. That's your clue to look for a typo.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: data = sorted([3, 1, 2, 9, 1]) … Caption: Prints 3.2 2
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In Python, sorted puts a list in order. The middle item is the median, and sum divided by len is the mean.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Bars start at zero; A title and units; Where the data came from.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Summaries need a chart beside them. Bars start at zero. Give the chart a title, and units on the axis. And say where the data came from.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Soil readings; Glitches out; Median: still.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, a week of soil readings with a few glitches. Leave them out, and see which summaries move. The lowest jumps from zero to about fifty-five, but the median doesn't move.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. Which of these makes a bar chart unfair?

scenes.visual: Summary card: Mean: add, divide; Median: the middle; Extremes drag the mean; Honest charts start at zero. Takeaway bar: Ask which summary, and look at the chart.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Bars that don't start at zero make small differences look huge. Remember: the mean adds and divides; the median is the middle. One extreme value drags the mean, not the median. And an honest chart starts at zero.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: An average in an advert; Mean or median?; What drags it?. Ms Salma beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: find an average in an advert or the news. Ask: is it a mean or a median? And what could be dragging it?

checkpoints.prompt: Marks of 11, 12, 13, 14, and one typed as 150. Which summary is still about right?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the median is 13, the middle mark. The typo drags the mean up to 40.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the mean and the total add in the 150. The median, the middle mark, stays at 13.

checkpoints.prompt: Which of these makes a bar chart unfair?

options.text: Bars that don't start at zero

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — cutting the axis makes small differences look huge.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — titles and labels help. Bars that don't start at zero make small differences look huge.
